reader_question: Where did federal spending go in fiscal 2026?
grade_line: Documented: the Treasury’s monthly statement of federal outlays
title: Social Security took the largest share of federal spending in fiscal 2026, $1,667.1 billion.
measure_line: Net federal outlays by budget function, billions of dollars, nominal, fiscal year 2026 (October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026), United States; each tile’s share is of the functions with positive outlays, $7,566.3 billion
notes: Eleven functions under 6 percent each fold into one tile, $1,089.8 billion in all; the table lists each.
Shares are of the 17 functions with positive outlays, $7,566.3 billion; net outlays came to $7,395.8 billion after two negative lines.
alt: Tiles sized by fiscal 2026 net outlays for each budget function with positive outlays. Social Security, $1,667.1 billion, is the largest, then Medicare, $1,072.6 billion, net interest, $1,051.8 billion, health, $1,025.6 billion, and national defense, $965.2 billion.

source_line: Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Monthly Treasury Statement, Table 9, outlays by function, fiscal 2026, United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Tiles show the functions with positive net outlays, $7,566.3 billion against total net outlays of $7,395.8 billion; offsetting receipts and Commerce and Housing Credit, both negative, are left out.
